answers.note: I think the current hashvatar result feels much more vibrant and alive. The mix across a guest list with no custom avatars looks beautiful. Even on an otherwise empty dashboard of ours, the color in the avatar brings a certain life to the page. Limiting to one palette like option 2, or the more muted tone of option 3, really drains a lot of life from the default avatars. Still open to new ideas beyond the current hashvatar, but not these directions here.

This does a good job of making the event page feel more social, not just a cloud storage folder album. As an additional note, we could run an exploration on how we're displaying metadata/metrics in both host and guest event heads. I'm going to mix some of these up across host vs guest, but the general idea is that we have a guest & view count below the event title, the guest count again in the guests action card, the media count to the far right of the activity bar, the media count again at the top left of the gallery below, etc. Feels very scattered, not a clean presentation, repeated info, etc. Whole head can be redesigned to fit. Also hate how the nav cuts the hero image slideshow harshly, how the hero slideshow is the only full width component (alignment feels weird - may look way better in an enclosed featured card, stacked directly above the actions row or something - leaving creativity up to you), etc.

This helps provide a more consistent interface and experience across host and guest dashboards, which should be the goal where possible. Should not feel like drastically different experiences, so users who function on both sides (as an event host, and as a guest to other events) has a more seamless experience switching across. Of course, each has its own features and enhancements.

I'd like to see another exploration of this. I like options 2 and 3 much more than option 1 right now, simply due to the fact that always applying the house ember will get very boring after a couple of events sharing the same visual look. Options 2 and 3 add a more experiential feel that varies across events. However, option 2's floating lamp in the mobile head feels a bit weird (draws the eye first as a useless artifact, before seeing any title/add/etc). Also, option 3's edge-to-edge visual looks amazing in the head (beautiful but allows the UI to take center stage, rather than fight for attention), but I think we should remove the desktop seam below because they're fighting each other. Think the seam in general is going to demand too much attention as is within the event page. Very curious what you come up with on your creative side, but none of these are winners as is.
